result.description:
Concrete Support Services (CSS) is a fully independent concrete testing and engineering consultancy supporting construction projects right across Melbourne. From our laboratory and field operations, we deliver concrete testing, materials assessment and technical advice that builders, contractors and engineers rely on to keep their projects moving and compliant. Because we operate as a completely independent laboratory, our clients know that every result we issue is backed by integrity, confidentiality and impartiality. Our work aligns with Australian Standards and NATA requirements, and our team combines decades of hands-on concrete technology expertise with a genuine commitment to service. What sets us apart is speed paired with accuracy we understand that critical site activities can’t wait, so we go out of our way to turn around reliable field and laboratory results promptly and to consistently exceed what our clients expect. As we continue to grow, we’re looking for a motivated Civil Engineering Technician to join our team at Oakleigh South and play a hands-on role in delivering the quality and responsiveness our clients count on.

Key Responsibilities
•	Carry out and coordinate a full program of on-site and in-laboratory tests on concrete, construction materials and soils including sampling fresh concrete, casting and curing specimens, slump and compressive strength testing all in accordance with Australian Standards.
•	Interpret job briefs, project specifications and work assignment instructions, then apply the appropriate testing procedures and select the correct equipment for each task.
•	Record, collate and analyse test results, perform the associated computations, and enter data accurately and promptly into our laboratory data-management systems so clients receive fast, dependable results.
•	Prepare technical sketches, charts, tabulations and test reports that support civil engineering works such as roads, drainage, water supply and sewerage reticulation systems, dams and structural elements where concrete and materials testing is required.
•	Conduct site inspections of concrete and civil works, and help organise and oversee sampling, re-testing and remedial or maintenance verification where required.
•	Estimate material quantities and associated costs, and check that materials and finished works comply with specifications, regulations and relevant contract provisions.
•	Collect field data during site surveys and sampling runs including on road, pavement and infrastructure projects and consolidate it for analysis and reporting.
•	Calibrate, maintain and correctly operate field and laboratory testing equipment, and keep clear records of its condition and use.
•	Uphold the laboratory’s quality management system and safeguard the integrity, impartiality and confidentiality of every result, in line with NATA and Australian Standards requirements.
•	Liaise professionally with clients, site supervisors and project engineers, providing clear technical support and rapid feedback to accommodate critical site timelines.
•	Support concrete mix design and quality-control activities, contributing observations and data that help clients meet their construction project needs.
•	Follow all workplace health and safety procedures and contribute to a safe, well-organised working environment both on site and in the laboratory.

About You
•	Strong attention to detail and a methodical, accurate approach to testing and record-keeping.
•	Reliable, punctual and able to manage priorities to meet time-critical site demands.
•	A team player who communicates clearly and professionally with colleagues and clients.
•	Committed to integrity, impartiality and confidentiality in all aspects of the work.
•	Safety-conscious, with a genuine respect for standards, procedures and compliance.
•	Physically capable of the practical, hands-on aspects of field and laboratory testing.
•	Willing to learn, take direction and grow within a supportive, quality-driven team.

Qualifications & Experience
•	An AQF Associate Degree, Advanced Diploma or Diploma in a relevant civil, engineering or materials-related discipline.
•	At least 1 year of relevant experience.

What We Offer
•	Salary:  $75,000 – $85,000 plus superannuation per annum.
•	Hours: Full-time position, typically 38 hours per week.
•	Location: Oakleigh South, VIC.

How to Apply
If this sounds like you, we’d love to hear from you. Please submit your resume together with a brief cover letter outlining your relevant experience and qualifications.

result.description:
## ICT Support Technician
## Position Overview
We are looking for a motivated and technically proficient ICT Support Technician to join our team and provide reliable support across our computer infrastructure, software systems, and web technologies. In this role, you will be responsible for diagnosing and resolving technical issues, maintaining hardware and software environments, and ensuring end users receive timely and effective assistance. The ideal candidate is a proactive problem-solver with strong communication skills and a genuine passion for technology. This position suits someone who thrives in a fast-paced environment and is committed to delivering high-quality technical support.
## Key Responsibilities
- Assess software and hardware requirements to identify appropriate technical solutions and resolve user-reported problems effectively.
- Respond promptly to enquiries from staff regarding software and hardware issues, providing clear guidance and practical resolutions in a professional manner.
- Install, configure, and maintain approved software applications, ensuring systems remain up to date, secure, and aligned with organisational standards.
- Adapt and modify existing programs and system configurations to better meet the evolving needs of end users and business operations.
- Implement, configure, and monitor computer networks, supporting both wired and wireless infrastructure to maintain consistent connectivity across the organisation.
- Design, update, and maintain organisational websites, ensuring content accuracy, functionality, and a positive user experience.
- Repair and replace peripheral equipment such as printers, terminals, monitors, and modems, maintaining accurate records of assets and service activity.
- Provide first- and second-level technical support to end users, either in person, remotely, or via a helpdesk or call centre environment, logging all incidents and resolutions through the appropriate ticketing system.
- Promote the efficient and effective use of applications and equipment across teams, offering training and guidance where required.
- Collaborate with internal stakeholders and external vendors to escalate and resolve complex technical issues in a timely manner.
- Conduct routine system checks, preventative maintenance, and performance monitoring to minimise downtime and ensure infrastructure reliability.
- Maintain thorough technical documentation, including user guides, network diagrams, and records of system configurations and changes.
## Required Qualifications & Skills
- Certificate III or IV in Information Technology, or a relevant tertiary qualification in ICT, Computer Science, or a related discipline.
- Demonstrated experience in a technical support, helpdesk, or IT operations role.
- Solid understanding of computer hardware components, operating systems (Windows, macOS, Linux), and common business software applications.
- Experience installing, configuring, and troubleshooting software and peripheral devices.
- Working knowledge of networking fundamentals, including TCP/IP, DNS, DHCP, and LAN/WAN connectivity.
- Familiarity with web technologies and basic website maintenance, including content management systems.
- Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with the ability to diagnose technical issues efficiently and accurately.
- Excellent verbal and written communication skills, with the ability to explain technical concepts clearly to non-technical users.
- Ability to manage competing priorities, work independently, and maintain composure under pressure.
- A customer-focused approach with a professional and courteous manner in all interactions.
## Preferred Qualifications
- CompTIA A+, Network+, or equivalent industry certification.
- ITIL Foundation certification or familiarity with ITIL service management principles.
- Experience working in a managed service provider (MSP) or enterprise IT environment.
- Exposure to cloud platforms such as Microsoft 365, Azure, or Google Workspace.
- Experience with remote desktop tools and helpdesk ticketing systems such as ServiceNow, Freshdesk, or Jira Service Management.
- Knowledge of cybersecurity best practices and endpoint protection solutions.
## Why Join Us?
- Be part of a collaborative and supportive team culture that values continuous learning and professional growth.
- Access ongoing training, certification support, and clear pathways for career advancement within the ICT field.
- Enjoy a stable, full-time permanent role with a competitive salary and superannuation package.
- Benefit from flexible working arrangements and a healthy work-life balance in a forward-thinking organisation.
- Work with modern technology and contribute to meaningful projects that directly support business operations and user experience.
## Job Details
- Job Type: Full-time, Permanent
- Work Schedule: 8-hour shift
- Salary: $70,000 – $120,000 per year + Super

result.description:
The Client 
Smart Energy Group is a full-service renewable solar energy company servicing Australia wide. They design and install bespoke solar solutions that reduce the energy costs of Australian households and businesses whilst improving Australia's green footprint.
They are seeking an experienced Office Manager to join their team Sydney, NSW.


The Role
The position is responsible for coordinating office personnel, allocating resources,
maintaining operational standards, managing records and reporting systems, and
ensuring effective communication between internal departments. The role also
contributes to workforce planning, process improvement, staff development, and
operational compliance to support business objectives.
This is a full-time position with an annual salary of $80,000 plus superannuation. 

The Responsibilities
•	Contribute to the planning, development and review of office services, procedures and operational standards
•	Establish priorities and service standards for sales administration and scheduling functions
•	Monitor operational workflows and implement process improvements to enhance efficiency
•	Ensure effective coordination between Sales, Operations, Installation and Administration departments
•	Allocate staffing resources, workloads and operational support based on business requirements
•	Coordinate office resources, equipment and systems to support business activities
•	Monitor team capacity and operational demands to ensure service delivery targets are met
•	Assign work tasks and monitor performance of scheduling and administration staff
•	Provide leadership, coaching, training and ongoing support to team members
•	Conduct performance reviews and contribute to performance management processes
•	Assist with recruitment, onboarding and training of new employees
•	Manage office records, operational documentation and reporting systems
•	Ensure accurate maintenance of business records, customer information and sales data
•	Oversee CRM systems, including Salesforce and Field Service Lightning
•	Maintain operational reporting and performance tracking systems
•	Oversee appointment scheduling processes and sales administration activities
•	Coordinate workforce schedules and operational requirements across multiple sales regions
•	Manage planning and logistics for away-trip operations and regional sales activities
•	Liaise with operational departments to align scheduling with installation capacity
•	Liaise with managers, operational teams and other professionals to coordinate business activities
•	Facilitate communication between departments and assist in resolving operational issues
•	Respond to internal stakeholder requests and support continuous business improvement initiatives
•	Ensure office equipment, systems and technology resources are maintained and operational
•	Coordinate system access, software requirements and operational support resources
•	Monitor office supply requirements and administrative resources
•	Ensure compliance with company policies, procedures and operational standards
•	Support adherence to relevant workplace health and safety requirements
•	Ensure business processes comply with privacy legislation and data management requirements
•	Assist with implementing regulatory and organisational compliance initiatives
•	Prepare operational reports and performance metrics for management review
•	Monitor scheduling efficiency, workload distribution and service delivery standards
•	Analyse operational trends and identify opportunities for process improvement
•	Provide recommendations to improve office productivity and operational performance


The Requirements:	
•	Must hold a minimum Degree qualification in Business Administration, Management, or a related field.
•	Minimum 3 years of experience in office administration, operations coordination, business support, scheduling or office management roles
•	Minimum 3 years’ experience as an Office Manager or in an office administration management role
•	At least 3 years’ experience coordinating office operations, administrative systems, and business support functions
•	Minimum 3 years’ experience managing records, schedules, correspondence, and operational documentation in a commercial environment
•	At least 3 years’ experience supporting multidisciplinary teams within property, real estate, or customer service environments
•	At least 3 years’ experience using office management systems, Microsoft Office applications, and business administration software
•	Strong knowledge of office administration procedures, workflow coordination, and document management practices
•	Ability to manage competing priorities and maintain operational efficiency in a fast-paced environment
•	Strong organisational, communication, and stakeholder coordination skills
•	Ability to prepare reports, maintain accurate records, and manage confidential information professionally
•	Good understanding of workplace compliance, administrative controls, and customer service standards
•	Ability to work independently and support business operations within structured deadlines
•	High attention to detail and problem-solving capability

result.description:
Location: Meningie, SA, 5264
Full-Time: Immediate start
Reports to: Aged Care Facility Manager
Job Title: Enrolled Nurse
Salary range: $79,500 - $85,000 + Superannuation
Job Closure date: 30 days

Job Summary:
Our client is a community-based not-for-profit home located in a small town of Meningie. Their modern, 30 bed home has a lovely outlook over the town and Lake. Our client is looking for an experienced Enrolled Nurse to join the team focussed on ensuring an excellent quality of care to residents and by extension, their families.

Key Responsibilities include:
• Assist in the assessment, planning, and implementation of resident care under RN supervision.
• Administer medications and treatments as prescribed, following facility protocols.
• Monitor and document residents’ health status, reporting changes to the RN.
• Assist with wound care, catheter management, and other clinical interventions.
• Support residents with activities of daily living (ADLs)
• Foster a person-centred approach, respecting residents’ dignity and preferences.
• Engage residents in social and recreational activities to enhance quality of life.
• Provide emotional support to residents and their families.
• Adhere to infection control, WHS, and aged care quality standards.
• Maintain accurate and timely documentation in care records.
• Follow facility policies, procedures, and regulatory requirements.
• Work effectively within a multidisciplinary team (RNs, carers, allied health).
• Participate in handovers, staff meetings, and training sessions.
• Mentor and support less experienced care staff as needed.

Qualifications & Requirements:
Essential:
• Diploma of Nursing (or equivalent) with current AHPRA registration as an Enrolled Nurse.
• At least 1 year experience in aged care, dementia care, or a similar setting (preferred).
• Strong clinical skills, including medication administration and chronic disease management.
• Understanding of Aged Care Quality Standards and person-centred care.
• Current First Aid & CPR certification.
• National Police Check and NDIS Worker Screening required.
• Must comply with having annual flu vaccination and be fully immunised against COVID-19.

Desirable:
• Experience with palliative care and complex health needs.
• Knowledge of electronic health records (e.g., iCare, MHR).
• Thrives within a great team environment.
• A desire for long-term employment.

Personal Attributes:
• Compassionate, patient, and empathetic.
• Strong communication and teamwork skills.
• Ability to work in a fast-paced environment with resilience.

How to Apply:
If you're passionate about quality aged care and meet the requirements, we'd love to hear from you!
*All successful applicants must comply with Aged Care Quality Standards and complete orientation training. *

Please submit your resume and a cover letter outlining your experience and why you'd be perfect for this role.
